text:
mira: Heads up — ACME just escalated: they need per-tenant routing policies + stronger multi-tenant isolation across regions. Asking for EU-only routing, hard isolation of KV cache, and fast failover. Can we scope this for next quarter? What are the right launch criteria and tradeoffs?

alex: who at ACME asked? any SLA numbers?

mira: @alex sales reported from the legal/security review. High level asks: 1) routing by tenant to region (EU-only) 2) KV/cache isolation (no cross-tenant hits) 3) auditable routing + routing-change rollback 4) <30s failover to backup region 5) optional on-prem later.

sam: +1 to prioritizing EU-only routing for compliance. For launch criteria I'd propose: must-haves = policy API, audit logs, failover test harness, docs; nice-to-have = per-tenant billing breakdown, on-prem package.

jordan: watch out: hard cache isolation will tank cache hit rates and raise token cost. If we shard cache by tenant you lose prefix reuse and batching locality. Also cross-region KV replication increases RTO unless we accept eventual consistency.

lee: propose phased plan: Phase A (Q2): soft routing policies + route preference + canary in eu-west; Phase B (Q3): tenant-aware cache slices with opt-in, audit trails, and automated rollback; Phase C (later): on-prem/VPC packaging and KMS tie-in. Launch criteria per phase: list below.

lee: Phase A must: API to attach policy to tenant, route preference enforcement, metrics exposed (route hit/miss), canary tooling, docs. Phase B must: KV isolation option, policy enforcement at edge, SLA docs, infra runbook, cost model. Phase C must: private control plane, KMS/HSM integration, enterprise rollout checklist.

alex: sample minimal policy model (for discussion):

```
route_policy:
  tenant: "acme"
  match: "tenant_id == 'acme'"
  preferred_region: "eu-west-1"
  fallbacks:
    - "eu-west-2"
    - "global"
  cache_mode: "isolated"  # options: shared | isolated | hybrid
```

alex: note: cache_mode=isolated implies dedicated shard or namespacing + higher cost. hybrid can give best-effort savings.

sam: for launch canary metrics: p95 latency, error rate, failover time, cache hit rate by tenant, per-tenant cost delta. Guardrails: rollback on >3% error delta or >20% cost delta.

jordan: operational concerns: automated rollback must revert routing and flush relevant KV namespaces. Need a simulated failover test in staging that completes in <30s. Also need tracing propagated with tenant tags.

infra-bot: RFC created: RFC-PLT-142 "Tenant routing + isolation slices" https://redwood.internal/rfcs/142 (cc @mira @alex)

mira: OK — agreed direction. Action items: 1) @alex to draft arch spec + perf impact estimates, 2) @lee to write phase-based PRD, 3) @sam to own launch criteria and canary plan, 4) @jordan to prototype failover test. I'll book triage with legal/sales next week.

sam: +1. Can we include a checklist for customer asks (EU residency, audit logs, isolation certs) so sales knows what to promise?

lee: yep — I'll add a customer-facing capability matrix to the PRD.

mira: thanks all — putting RFC link in the PRD. If anyone has objections to the phased plan please reply by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
